story: Aunt May lives **above** a bank. Her **address** is 12 Green Street.
One morning, Aunt May asks Ben his **age**.
“I’m nine,” says Ben.
Ben is **afraid** of dark rooms. But **after** breakfast, Aunt May asks him for help.
“My toy bear is missing. Are **all** the children here?”
“**All right**,” says Ben. “We can look for it. You **always** put it on your bed.”
Then **another** child arrives. It is Lily.
“Do you have **any** idea where the bear is?” Lily asks.
The children meet **at** the stairs. Their **aunt** is tired, but she is still **awake**.
First, they look at the **back** of the house. The weather is **bad**. Billy the puppy walks **badly** because his leg hurts, but he still wants to play.
Billy runs onto the **balcony**. A music **band** is playing across the road, near the **bank**.
Then Billy runs into the **basement**.
Ben stops at the door. “There is a **bat** in there!”
“It is **called** Bob,” says Aunt May. “Bob is friendly.”
Ben looks again. On the wall, there is also a picture of a **bear** with a long **beard**.
The children laugh **because** it looks funny.
**Before** they go upstairs, Lily looks **below** a chair.
“I found the **best** clue!” she says.
Ben looks **behind** a box. “My clue is even **better**.”
He finds a blue **blanket**. On it, there is some yellow hair from a doll with **blond** hair.
“This search is not **boring**,” says Lily.
They **both** hear Billy upstairs.
At the **bottom** of the stairs, there is a water **bottle** and Billy’s dog **bowl**.
Billy runs past them. He hits the bowl, and it **breaks**.
“Please **bring** Billy back!” calls Aunt May.
Billy runs past the **bus station** and stops at the **bus stop**. The road is very **busy**, so he cannot cross it.
“We must **buy** Billy a new bowl,” says Ben.
Then Lily sees something **by** the river.
Aunt May’s toy bear is sitting on a bench.
Billy sits next to the bear and moves his tail.
Aunt May smiles. “Billy did not want to lose the bear,” she says. “He only wanted to take his friend for a walk.”

reading: Read 1 - You read the story out loud. The child only listens. No dictionary.
Read 2 - Stop at every dark word. Let the child guess it from the picture in the story.
Read 3 - Ask the five questions. Short answers are fine.
Read 4 - The child retells the story in four sentences.
teaching: smell / feel / look are linking verbs, so they take an adjective: the puppy smells bad, not smells badly.
badly says HOW you do an action: Billy walks badly, Billy sings badly.
blond is used for hair, so we say a doll with blond hair, not a blond doll.
be called gives a name, so give the bat a real name: it is called Bob.
